# Sipat

> Sipat ("Gabay kahit walang signal") is a free, offline-first typhoon companion for Filipino households on budget Android phones. It turns the PAGASA warning a family heard on the radio into a checklist fitted to that household, and answers questions in Taglish only from official preparedness guides bundled in the app (PAGASA, NDRRMC and OCD, DOH, PHIVOLCS, BFP), with the source one tap away.

Key facts:

- Works fully offline (airplane mode): household setup, phases, warnings, checklists, Ask in Taglish, hotlines and the bundled guide. The network is used only on a user action while the app is open.
- Three bagyo phases: Bago ang bagyo (before), Habang may bagyo (during), Pagkatapos ng bagyo (after). The phase changes the theme, the checklist and the answers.
- Warnings covered: PAGASA tropical cyclone wind signals 1 to 5, rainfall warnings, storm surge and gale warnings.
- Grounded answers only: a search gate runs before the model; when nothing matches, the app says "Wala ito sa gabay" and the model is never called.
- Useful without AI: the vetted summary always shows first. Llama 3.2 1B Instruct (Q4_K_M, about 0.81 GB) runs on the phone via llama.rn to rephrase it, and is an optional one-time download.
- Safety in code: intent routing, an answer verifier and phase switching are enforced in code. Hotlines, evacuation centers and PAGASA bulletin data are rendered from data, never generated by the model.
- Private by design: no mandatory account, no analytics SDKs, no background services. Family names, face photos and location stay on the phone. Face detection only crops photos; there is no face recognition.
- Business model: households never pay; local government units (LGUs) pay for a localized pack with their evacuation centers, hotlines and advisories.
- Stack: Expo (React Native New Architecture), TypeScript, MiniSearch (BM25+) retrieval with Taglish synonyms, react-native-mmkv, Ed25519-signed feed.
- Stage: built as a 10-hour hackathon MVP, then planned for an LGU pilot. Android first.
